standard.title: Develop characters and dramatic action
standard.description: develop characters and situations, and shape and sustain dramatic action to communicate ideas, perspectives and/or meaning in improvised, devised and/or scripted forms
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can improvise and devise drama using elements of drama to communicate ideas and meaning (Y3-4). They can shape improvisations using voice, movement and language, and devise drama collaboratively with communicative intent.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students develop characters and situations, and shape and sustain dramatic action to communicate ideas, perspectives and/or meaning in improvised, devised and/or scripted forms.

nodes.label: Developing character
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can develop a character with consistent physical, vocal and relational qualities, distinguishable from their own default behaviour.
nodes.minimum_width: Student creates and sustains one character across a short scene, making at least two distinct characterisation choices (voice and physicality).
nodes.typical_width: Students explore physical, fictional or emotional spaces to create characters; they vary voice (projection, dynamics, pace, pause, pitch) and use movement and gesture to communicate characters' intentions; they rehearse and negotiate with others to interpret scripts and create characters and their relationships.
wider: Students use empathy to develop characters from different perspectives, considering situations from multiple characters' viewpoints and challenging stereotypes
Students develop a 'new scene' to include in a dramatic re-telling of a known narrative, creating a character who was not in the original
nodes.hinge_reason: Consistent character development is the anchor for sustaining dramatic action; if characters collapse under pressure (breaking in and out of role or losing character consistency), the dramatic action cannot be sustained across longer or more complex forms — particularly in scripted drama.

response_modes.reason: Character consistency develops through rehearsal and deliberate practice; students need repeated opportunities to 'inhabit' a character across different scenarios before they can sustain it through a full drama.

Developing characters across different contexts — improvised, scripted, empathy-based, culturally situated — builds transferable characterisation skills and prevents students from defaulting to a single character type.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The range of character types, cultural perspectives, dramatic forms and relationship dynamics available is very broad; students who develop characters across many contexts build substantially richer performance range.
success_criteria: Student creates a character distinguishable from their own default through at least two consistent choices (voice and physical)
Student sustains character across a scene including during reactions to others
Student can describe the character's perspective or intention

nodes.label: Shaping dramatic action across forms
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can shape dramatic action — developing situation, tension and resolution — across improvised, devised and/or scripted forms.
nodes.minimum_width: Student shapes a dramatic sequence with an identifiable beginning, complication and resolution across one form.
nodes.typical_width: Students shape and sustain dramatic action across improvised, devised and/or scripted drama; they use rehearsal, interaction and negotiation with others; they use props, costumes and available technologies (light, sound, multimedia) as dramatic symbols; they develop drama for school rituals or community events with a specific purpose.
wider: Students devise drama based on research about a school or local community project, using drama to present different perspectives in a debate or issue
Students explore how a devised drama for a specific community audience (e.g. school assembly, cultural ceremony) requires adapting form and content to purpose
Students use Viewpoints to frame questions about their own drama: 'How did the performers use elements effectively?', 'What was the purpose?'

response_modes.reason: Shaping sustained dramatic action across forms is the integration point — character, situation, tension, purpose and audience awareness all converge. Structured reflection and feedback during rehearsal is the key scaffold.

success_criteria: Student shapes a dramatic sequence with a recognisable dramatic arc (beginning, complication, resolution)
Student demonstrates sustained dramatic action across a complete piece in at least one form
Student can articulate what idea, perspective or meaning the drama is communicating
